mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thereby driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following a low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5% signals labor market weakness, which may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods after UNRATE exceeds 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) increases while unemployment (UNRATE) also rises, it may indicate structural issues in the labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods when PAYEMS and UNRATE move inversely, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) during a late-cycle expansion signals reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day periods following an INDPRO decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in real consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates strong demand, which may boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods following RSAFS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1600 indicates a slowdown in the housing market, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day periods after HOUST drops below 1600, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising and GDP (GDPC1) growth is slowing, it creates a restrictive monetary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 30% of the 60-day periods when FEDFUNDS rises and GDPC1 slows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) during a monetary tightening cycle may reduce liquidity and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day periods after FEDFUNDS increases, the hypothesis is rejected.
